claims.text: PLD-grown AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles on silicon nitride are initially metastable FCC particles.
The initial particles are sub-5 nm and can have elliptical, icosahedral, or truncated-octahedral geometries.
Surface-energy gradients override sluggish diffusion in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Thermodynamic driving forces can produce elemental phase separation in multicomponent alloys.
Local atomic-radius misfit creates element-dependent diffusion behavior in high-entropy alloys.
Au and Cu preferentially migrate to the nanoparticle surface because they are low-melting-point constituents.
Surface-segregated Au and Cu subsequently evaporate.
The Gibbs-free-energy reduction from Au/Cu surface segregation becomes larger than the entropic stabilization of the bulk FCC phase at elevated temperature.
High surface energy lowers the diffusion activation barrier for Au and Cu in small AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Diffusion barriers can differ substantially among elements rather than being uniform throughout a high-entropy alloy.
Sluggish diffusion in a high-entropy matrix can be associated with elevated activation energies.
A critical temperature exists above which Au/Cu segregation and evaporation rates increase sharply.
Au/Cu segregation and evaporation cause rapid loss of sub-5 nm particles and widening or shifting of the particle-size distribution.
The surviving particles become spherical to minimize surface energy.
The FCC structure persists only while the surface is enriched in Pt, Ni, and Co and destabilizes after sufficiently large surface-composition changes.
Surface-energy terms dominate bulk thermodynamic terms only for particles smaller than 10 nm.
Particles smaller than 10 nm have a surface-to-volume ratio greater than 50%.
Icosahedral and truncated-octahedral particles have different critical segregation temperatures because their facet energies differ.
Thermally induced magnetic effects can alter entropy, internal energy, and phase free energies in Co-containing multicomponent alloys.
The proposed surface-driven mechanism should fail in bulk alloys or larger nanoparticles, where bulk diffusion kinetics and configurational entropy dominate.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis alternately says surface-energy gradients bypass sluggish-diffusion barriers, lower the diffusion activation barrier, and act alone without kinetic barriers. The proposed simulation then retains artificially sluggish diffusion and interprets any segregation as proof that surface energy alone is sufficient. Segregation still requires atomic mobility, so these formulations are not mechanistically equivalent.

The mechanism predicts initial surface enrichment in Au and Cu, whereas the outcome conditions FCC persistence on surface enrichment in Pt, Ni, and Co. A sequential transition after Au/Cu evaporation could reconcile these statements, but that sequence is not explicitly specified.
